- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion or lower volatility.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.2) or neutral (0.0–0.4), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is trending up.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) are common; cap forecast peaks at 1–2% below recent high or 1.5x recent average.
- Model frequently overreacts to sentiment shifts; lag correction: if sentiment changes sharply, delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate mid-term trends; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per 10-day window if sentiment is mixed or declining.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “high-low” cycles (e.g., 0.8 → 0.0 → 0.6), model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply smoothing or decay filter to forecast.
